- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 10-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% bias to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model lags in adjusting; delay correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual downward shift.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average before final output.
